params.body:
The vehicle list fits a laptop screen

The row actions were unreachable. Measured on production at a 1084px window: the
table asks 1433px inside a 992px container, and html and body carry
overflow-x: hidden, so those 441px are cut off with no scrollbar at all. The cell
holding view, duplicate, edit and delete sat at 1305 to 1475, entirely off-screen,
reachable by nothing. The card layout only starts at 767px, so every window
between 768px and roughly 1525px was affected, which is most laptops.

Widening the container was not available: an overflow container breaks the
quick-actions menu and the sticky header, both documented in this file from
earlier attempts. So the table itself had to shrink.

A table never renders below its min-content width and max-width cannot force it,
so every rule here works by lowering that minimum. They were measured together
rather than one at a time, because hiding a column lets the others expand: on its
own, hiding "gepubliceerd" appeared to make the table 133px WIDER, and four hides
together were worse than one.

What buys the 441px: the vehicle and price sub-lines may wrap, the status cell
loses width: 100%, the photo goes to 60px, the fixed width of the button column is
released, and the portal icons ride over each other like stacked avatars, which
turns 152px of icons into 97px with a white ring keeping each readable.

That leaves the four buttons of the last column, worth 146px, which is the one
thing that does not fit. Below 1550px they give way to the same four actions in
the quick-actions menu beside them, so nothing is lost, only moved. Above it the
buttons stay and the menu does not repeat them.

Verified in the browser against production at 1084px, with these rules exactly as
written and no !important: 1433 to 992, the actions column back in view at 1014,
and no sideways page scroll. The row grows from 76px to 104px, which is the price
of keeping every column.
params.title: The vehicle list fits a laptop screen
